daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Former President Joko Widodo appeared before the East Jakarta District Court on Thursday as a witness in a defamation case filed against political commentator Roy Suryo over allegations of a fake diploma. Jokowi told the court his current occupation is "entrepreneur" and detailed his educational history from primary school through his undergraduate degree at Gadjah Mada University, stating he brought all original diploma documents to the hearing. The presiding judge reminded Jokowi to answer questions firmly, while approximately 7,000 supporters gathered outside the courthouse.

  • Golkar politician Dasco Bisowarno dismissed allegations linking him to an illegal wiretapping case, calling reports that he would be named vice presidential candidate a hoax intended to distract from the wiretapping controversy.
  • Former President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono expressed concern about the state of Indonesian politics, warning that all means are being justified in pursuit of power.
  • The DPR's Commission III stated that the draft Asset Forfeiture Bill reinforces that corrupt officials can be sentenced to death, as legislators begin formal discussions on the legislation.
  • Indonesian Judges Association (PII) urged tighter judicial oversight provisions in the draft Asset Forfeiture Bill currently being debated.
  • DPR member Zulfikar Achmad, the oldest legislator in parliament, passed away on Thursday.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The chiefs of the Indonesian and Singaporean air forces jointly conducted an F-16 patrol flight on Thursday in a display of bilateral defence cooperation. The operation underscores ongoing military collaboration between the two Southeast Asian neighbours. Indonesia has been strengthening its defence ties across the region amid evolving security challenges.

  • Indonesia is boosting its digital defence capabilities to counter foreign military recruitment targeting Indonesian citizens online.
  • Foreign Minister Sugiono called for solid APEC cooperation to bolster Asia-Pacific regional resilience at the economic forum.
  • The Indonesian Consulate General in Karachi recorded $9.4 million in potential cooperation at the Textile Exhibition International 2026 in Pakistan.
  • Australia is providing aerial assistance to extinguish forest fires in East Kalimantan in a seven-day air operation.

Other

Indonesia is targeting 80-percent electric bus adoption by 2030 as part of its push toward sustainable transportation. The government is urging expansion of the intermediate manufacturing sector to support industrial deepening and supply chain development. Indonesia also pushed for a fair energy transition and global support at COP31 climate negotiations.

  • Broiler chicken farmers are demanding government intervention after prices plummeted sharply in recent weeks.
  • Indonesia reported 401,586 respiratory illness cases linked to forest fires, as the wildfire season continues to impact public health across multiple provinces.
  • The Palembang waste-to-energy project has entered the commissioning phase, marking progress in South Sumatra's renewable energy infrastructure.
  • Antam's gold buyback price jumped by Rp 13,000 on Thursday, while spot prices edged slightly higher.
  • The government set a target of 2,121 home renovations in Surakarta and Padang under its housing improvement programme.
